default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-938.title: Round-number rejection
E-938.hypothesis: Index levels at round thousands/halves attract resting orders and stops; a bar that pokes through a round number and closes back on the original side is a failed attempt to cross it, so fade it.

E-939.title: Double top/bottom test
E-939.hypothesis: A second test of the session extreme after a pullback, ending in a bar against the extreme, shows the first push was not absorbed by new aggressors; fade the second test.

E-941.title: Stale extreme break
E-941.hypothesis: A session high/low untouched for a long time holds stops of those who faded it; a close through it forces covering and follows through.

E-942.title: Trend-to-noise cross
E-942.hypothesis: A regression slope large relative to price dispersion marks a clean directional drift; its first crossing of a threshold flags orderly flow that tends to persist.

E-943.title: Efficiency-ratio chop fade
E-943.hypothesis: When Kaufman's efficiency ratio is low the market is moving sideways without net direction; an extreme of the window in that regime is an excursion that mean-reverts.

E-944.title: OBV divergence fade
E-944.hypothesis: A new price extreme not confirmed by signed cumulative volume means the push lacked aggressive flow; fade it.

E-945.title: Floor-pivot offset rejection
E-945.hypothesis: Levels at fixed fractions of yesterday's range around the pivot are widely tracked by floor-pivot users; a poke and close back is a failed attempt, fade it.

E-946.title: Wick cluster rejection
E-946.hypothesis: Several bars in a short window closing far from their highs (or lows) show repeated rejection by the other side; trade against the rejected direction.

E-947.title: Stochastic extreme re-entry
E-947.hypothesis: When the close falls back from the top (or rises from the bottom) of its recent range, momentum buyers (sellers) are losing control; fade the re-entry.
